title: kith-events: reconnect with last-event-id replay
description:
What: Add Last-Event-ID reconnect replay to the EventSource handler so clients that briefly disconnect are notified of state changes they missed.

Algorithm:
1. In events_handler (kith-events/src/lib.rs), extract TypedHeader<LastEventId> from request parts (axum headers crate) OR extract via HeaderMap lookup:
   let last_event_id = headers.get("last-event-id").and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()).map(str::to_owned);
2. If last_event_id is Some:
   a. Validate length <= 64 bytes; if longer treat as absent (do not error)
   b. Validate format: must be "s-" followed by digits only (regex "^s-[0-9]+$"); if invalid treat as absent
   c. Lock store: let store_guard = state.store.lock().await
   d. Read current states:
      let contact_state = store_guard.contacts().get_state()?
      let chat_state = store_guard.chats().get_state()?
      let msg_state = store_guard.messages().get_state()?
   e. drop(store_guard)  // release lock before building stream
   f. For each (type_name, current_state) in [("Contact",contact_state),("Chat",chat_state),("Message",msg_state)]:
      - If types filter includes type_name AND current_state != last_event_id:
        - Prepend to stream: emit SSE event for this type with current_state
3. Subscribe to broadcast channel AFTER releasing store lock (to avoid missing events between read and subscribe: subscribe first, then read states and prepend, so the live stream catches any concurrent state advance)

Correct ordering to avoid race:
  a. let rx = state.events_tx.subscribe()  // subscribe FIRST
  b. lock store, read states, unlock
  c. build replay_events vec
  d. chain(replay_events).chain(broadcast_stream)

Defensive rules:
- Subscribe to broadcast BEFORE reading store state to ensure no events lost during replay construction
- Validate Last-Event-ID before any DB access
- Never interpolate Last-Event-ID into SQL; parse to i64 then compare against get_state() return
- Invalid Last-Event-ID silently treated as absent (no 400 - client recovery is more important)
- Size limit on Last-Event-ID: silently ignore if > 64 bytes
